Write your audit to `audit.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your auditor skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.

head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2010 — corpus_sha256 re-opens the file by path (no O_NOFOLLOW) after read_regular already read it
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:536 — poslist nulls the whole defects_missed_pm3_v1 list when one v1-only id's position exceeds defects_seeded

---
name: audit
description: Security and quality audit of application codebase
role: review
effort: medium
allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, WebFetch, WebSearch, Bash(.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh *), Bash(br sync --import-only), Bash(br sync --flush-only), Bash(br comments add *), Bash(br label add *), Bash(.claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob *)
disallowed-tools:
  - NotebookEdit
capabilities:
  schema_version: 1
  read_files: true
  search_code: true
  write_files: true
  execute_commands:
    allowed:
      - command: ".claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["sync", "--import-only"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["sync", "--flush-only"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["comments", "add", "*"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["label", "add", "*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh"

        args: ["*"]

    deny_raw_shell: true
  web_access: true
  user_interaction: false
  agent_spawn: false
  task_management: false
cost-profile: heavy
context: fork
parallel_threshold: 2000
audit_categories: 5
timeout_minutes: 60
zones:
  system:
    path: .claude
    permission: none
  state:

<input_guardrails>
<!-- @skill-include: start input_guardrails | hash:957e7f01 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/input_guardrails.md -->
## Pre-Execution Guardrails (mechanized)

Run only if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob guardrails.input.enabled false` prints `true`
and env `LOA_GUARDRAILS_ENABLED` is not `false`: write the prompt/args to a temp file (Write tool), then run
`.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill auditing-security --mode ${LOA_RUN_MODE:-interactive} --file <temp-file>`

| Outcome | Action |
|---------|--------|
| JSON `action: "BLOCK"` | HALT; report the script's `reason` to the user |
| JSON `action: "PROCEED"` or `"WARN"` | Continue (the script logs) |
| Script missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output | Continue (fail-open) |

Never pass prompt text as a bash argv (quote-blindness FP class) — always via `--file`.
<!-- @skill-include: end input_guardrails -->
</input_guardrails>

# Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor

<objective>
Audit code, architecture, infrastructure or sprint implementations for security and quality; produce prioritized findings with actionable remediation at the output path for the audit type.
</objective>

<zone_constraints>
## Zone Constraints

Three-Zone Model per CLAUDE.loa.md: `.claude/` system = never edit (use `.claude/overrides/` or `.loa.config.yaml`); `grimoires/loa/`, `.beads/` state = read/write; this skill's app zone (`src/`, `lib/`, `app/`) = **Read-only**.

Scope: app-zone files less the `.reviewignore` patterns (read it); `.claude/`, `grimoires/`, `.beads/` and `.run/` are excluded unless `--no-reviewignore` is passed.
</zone_constraints>

<integrity_precheck>
<!-- @skill-include: start integrity_precheck | hash:47b71a70 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/integrity_precheck.md -->
## Integrity Pre-Check (MANDATORY)

Before ANY operation, verify System Zone integrity:

1. Check config: read `integrity_enforcement` in `.loa.config.yaml`
2. If `strict` and drift detected -> **HALT** and report
3. If `warn` -> Log warning and proceed with caution
<!-- @skill-include: end integrity_precheck -->
</integrity_precheck>

<factual_grounding>
<!-- @skill-include: start factual_grounding | hash:edec7c58 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/factual_grounding.md -->
## Factual Grounding (MANDATORY)

Before ANY synthesis, planning, or recommendation:

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`
3. **Flag assumptions**: Prefix ungrounded claims with `[ASSUMPTION]`

**Grounded Example:**
```
The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```
[ASSUMPTION] The database likely needs connection pooling
```
<!-- @skill-include: end factual_grounding -->
</factual_grounding>

<context_discipline>
<!-- @skill-include: start context_discipline | hash:8b81d75a | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/context_discipline.md -->
## Context Discipline

Class: `.run/context-class` (`long` default; `standard` via `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard` or a
≤200K model). `.claude/protocols/tool-result-clearing.md` — long 20K/50K/30K/150K, standard 2K/5K/3K/15K (single /
accumulated / full file / session) → extract ≤10 files, ≤20 words, file:line to NOTES.md; reason
from it. Big files: `notes-guard.sh read --file F --section <H>` / `--index` first. Start: NOTES.md
"Session Continuity"; end / pre-compaction: update it.
<!-- @skill-include: end context_discipline -->
</context_discipline>

<trajectory_logging>
<!-- @skill-include: start trajectory_logging | hash:e809010f | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/trajectory_logging.md -->
## Trajectory Logging

Log each significant step to `grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory/{agent}-{date}.jsonl`:

```

</trajectory_logging>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

## Factual Grounding (MANDATORY)

Before ANY synthesis, planning, or recommendation:

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`
3. **Flag assumptions**: Prefix ungrounded claims with `[ASSUMPTION]`

```
The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```
[ASSUMPTION] The database likely needs connection pooling
```

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md
**Change under review:** `pr/head.diff` — cycle-131 sprint-263 (closed review-catch mount, grader 1.3.0, oracle detector, dissent line anchors + budget_scale, row writer 1.4, report 1.3), 35 files

---

## Overall Assessment

The PR is large but well-tested in the parts it tests: the numeric-anchor normaliser, the budget scaling, the overlay/check core, the row writer and the report partitions each ship with bats coverage, and the cross-model dissent produced no rejected payloads. The adversarial-review.sh changes are sound (the estimate is integer, the config guard precedes the new reads, the schema-enforced branch holds the anchor to the same rule).

Two defects block merge. First, the closed-mount wiring in `pipeline-run.sh` records the overlay digests, then runs the arm toggles, then verifies the surface against those digests; the `effort` toggle rewrites every `SKILL.md` frontmatter and `model-config.yaml`, so arm `a7_effort_medium` is refused at launch on any review-catch PR whose answer set contains such a file (the auditing-security skill, which carries `effort:`, is in the pr-04 answer set the PR's own test names). Second, the 1.3.0 same-scope rule's Python end-of-definition detection ends a function at the `):` of a multi-line signature, so black-formatted functions (206 in `.claude/adapters` alone) get no scope clause at all.

The implementation report is the PR title and a file count; it carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough and no test-run evidence (I could not run the PR's bats suites: `pr/` holds only touched files, not the fixtures they load). That is an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED under this skill's rules and is recorded as a MEDIUM below.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Closed mount — toggles mutate answer paths after the digests are recorded

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:566` — `apply_arm_toggles` runs after `overlay_answer_paths` (:559) wrote `overlay_sha256=` lines, and `check_mount_closed` (:577) then compares the sandbox to those lines; the `effort` toggle (`head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:358-371`) rewrites every `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter in place (`_sm_strip_frontmatter_effort`, :261-272) and `.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml`, so clause (c) at `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:986` reports `mount_mutated=<path>` and `lib_call` turns it into `infrastructure_error` before any phase.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:566` (order), `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:358` (mutation), `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:986` (refusal)
**Issue:** Arm `a7_effort_medium` has `task_types: [all]` (`head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:89`), so on every review-catch task it goes overlay → effort toggle → check. Any answer path that is a `SKILL.md` with an `effort:` frontmatter line (6 of 37 skills in this tree, including `auditing-security/SKILL.md`, which the PR's own AG-50 test says is in pr-04's answer set: "d5: the audit skill reads its own later SKILL.md") or `.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml` has a post-toggle sha that differs from the recorded one while the recorded one equals the fixture's, which is exactly the clause (c) branch. The same class applies to `karpathy_block` (`CLAUDE.loa.md`, `constraints.json`), `rule_files` and `audit_delta_instruction` should an arm ever carry them on a review-catch task. The only test of toggle/overlay interaction (`head/evals/tests/sandbox-mount.bats:5096`) uses `dissent: false`, which edits `.loa.config.yaml` outside the answer set.
**Why This Matters:** A7 on review-catch becomes a guaranteed `infrastructure_error` for every task whose PR touches a skill with an effort line, with no phase run and no row that reads as a model result; the pre-registered A7 contrast silently loses those cells. The PR header comment ("the checked surface is the launched one") describes the ordering as intended, so this is a design conflict, not a typo.
**Required Fix:** Either (a) record the `overlay_sha256` baseline after `apply_arm_toggles` (re-run the digest step, or have `check_mount_closed` accept a toggle-declared exemption list for paths a toggle lawfully rewrote, recording `overlay_toggled=<path>` evidence), or (b) apply the effort/karpathy/rule/audit-delta toggles to answer paths only through the overlay source (i.e. make the toggle operate on the fixture copy so the digest reflects it), and add a bats case: overlay → `{"effort":"medium"}` on a fixture whose answer set includes a `SKILL.md` with `effort:` → `check_mount_closed` passes.

### 2. Grader 1.3.0 — Python scope ends at a multi-line signature

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:308` — `close_line` for Python returns at the first later non-blank, non-comment line indented no deeper than the `def`; for `def f(\n    a,\n):` the `):` line has the def's indentation, so the definition ends on the signature and the whole body is top-level (scope `None`), and clause (ii) of `hit_new` never credits a citation inside it.
**File:** `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:302-309`
**Issue:** Raised by the dissent as DISS-002 and confirmed by reading: `PY_HDR` (:213) matches `def NAME(` without requiring the closing paren, and the end detection does not track parentheses. `.claude/adapters` has 206 functions written this way (black style), and the review corpus is Loa PRs that touch them. A defect site inside such a body and a valid citation 4+ lines away inside the same function credit nothing under `recall` (the decision statistic), while `recall_pm3` is unaffected, so the rule's documented contract (header :422-460) is false for this common shape. The RG-37 test only covers one-line `def` headers.
**Why This Matters:** `recall` feeds `defect_catch_rate`, the pre-registered decision statistic of report 1.3; a systematic under-credit on a common code shape makes the "same scope" clause misreport exactly where it was meant to help.
**Required Fix:** In `close_line` (python), skip signature lines until the line containing the `):` (or `) -> T:`) that closes the header's open paren count before applying the dedent test; add an RG case with a multi-line signature and a citation 6 lines into the body.

---

## Observations

### 1. Budget scaling (dissent DISS-001, triaged MEDIUM)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:179` — `budget_cents_max // 600` turns an explicit YAML `false` into 600 before the whole-number check at :180, so `budget_scale: diff` with `budget_cents_max: false` keeps diff scaling capped at 600 instead of falling back to `fixed` as the example config (:395-396) and ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md promise. The file already notes the `//` pitfall for `companion_voice` (:212). The dissent rated this BLOCKING; the damage is bounded by the 600c default, so I hold it at MEDIUM.
**Suggestion:** read the raw value with `| tag` as `_adv_conf_budget_scale` does for the scale, and treat anything but `!!null`/absent and a valid `!!int` as malformed.

### 2. Row writer 1.4 reads the agent-writable config (dissent DISS-C-005)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:394` — `dissent_absent_reason` classifies a gate as `disabled` (a planned absence the report never excludes) from `sandbox/.loa.config.yaml`, which the agent can edit mid-run; the grader header in the same PR calls the sandbox tamperable. An in-run flip of `flatline_protocol.enabled` both suppresses the gate and records the absence as planned.
**Suggestion:** derive `disabled` from harness evidence only (`dissent=false`, `flatline=off`, `gates=false` lines in `meta/arm-evidence.txt`), or trust the sandbox config only when `loa_config_sha256` at finish equals the materialised one.

### 3. Oracle detector — `2>&1` splits the segment

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2159` — `split_segments` splits on a bare `&`, so `diff pr/head/X .claude/X 2>&1 | wc -l` becomes the segments `diff … 2>`, `1`, `wc -l`; the diff segment's separator is `;`, the pipe-sink check in `oracle_plan` (:2481) is skipped, and the result `4` (not an `ERR_LINE`, no ranges) marks every defect of the file `exposed_unknown` at :2420. AG-48's `| wc -l` case passes only without the redirection.
**Suggestion:** treat `N>&M`, `&>` and `>&` as part of the word in `split_segments` (only `&&` and a lone `&` followed by whitespace/newline are separators).

### 4. Process — no AC verification, no test evidence

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md:1` — the implementation report is the PR title and "35 file(s) in scope"; no `## AC Verification`, no `file:line` evidence per criterion, no statement that the ten touched/added bats suites ran green. The sprint's single task is the PR itself, so this is the only place the engineer could have shown the suites pass; I could not run them here (`pr/` lacks the fixture trees the suites load).
**Suggestion:** add the walkthrough and paste the bats summary lines (`eval-recall-grader`, `ablation-grade`, `ablation-row`, `ablation-report`, `sandbox-mount`, `took-effect`, `pipeline-run`, `run-ablation`, `adversarial-review-normalise`, `adversarial-review-budget-scale`).

### 5. Complexity

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2312` — `SIMPLICITY[shrink]`: `oracle_scan` is ~120 lines with four nested loops and inner closures; `oracle_plan` (:2435, ~65 lines) and `cmd_check` in `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:958` (~100 lines, clauses (a)–(d) in one body) are over the 50-line guideline with no justification comment. Over-engineering pass: the only redundancy found is the double read in `corpus_sha256` (below); `net: -4 lines possible`.
**Suggestion:** split `oracle_scan` into `later_lines(f)`, `scan_diff_result(...)` and `scan_read_result(...)`; split `cmd_check` per clause.

### 6. Grader 1.3.0 scope heuristics (low)

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:214` — `MD_HDR` treats any `#` line as a heading, including `# comment` lines inside fenced code blocks in `.md` files, which splits a section at a code comment and loses same-section credit for citations after it.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:287` — (dissent DISS-C-003, confirmed) `CLOSE_ONE` is searched on the whole header line, so a trailing comment holding a `}` (e.g. `f() {  # reads ${X}`) makes the function one line long and its body top-level. No such header exists in the head tree today.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:299` — bash `close_line` compares raw indentation (`len(t) - len(t.lstrip())`) while `headers` uses `expandtabs(8)` (:283); a tab-indented function never matches its closing brace and its scope runs to the next header.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:143` — (dissent DISS-C-004) `json.load` on the v1 manifest has no error handling: a malformed `v1/<fixture>.json` is a traceback and exit 1 rather than the header's exit 2 + `err()` JSON. Not a scoring risk: `grade_recall` (`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1639`) raises `GradeError` on the empty stdout.
- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:135` — the head-dir fallback `$workspace/pr/head` is the agent-writable sandbox copy; it is reached only when `EVAL_HEAD_DIR` is unset and the corpus fixture dir is absent, which `grade_recall` (:1631) leaves unset when `resolve_pr_fixture` fails. Defensive: refuse rather than fall back.

### 7. adversarial-review.sh (low)

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:164` — (dissent DISS-C-001) a yq failure yields `unreadable`, which is not the absent case, so an unparseable config sets `CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET=true`, logs a WARN about a key never written, and puts budget metadata in the envelope, against the "absent key is byte for byte the shipped envelope" contract.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:180` — `budget_cents_max: 0` passes the regex; under `diff` every run then refuses with `budget_exceeded` (fail-closed, but worth a WARN).
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/schemas/adversarial-finding.schema.json:248` — (dissent DISS-C-002) `metadata` has `additionalProperties: false` and the PR adds three budget keys but not the `reason` key the SET branch now writes (`head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:4445`); `status` also lacks `budget_exceeded` (pre-existing). The `anchor_line` description omits the 10,000,000 cap the normaliser applies.

### 8. Harness plumbing (low)

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:356` — `resolve_fixture` with `--task-yaml` tries four roots but not `$SOURCE_TREE/evals/fixtures/<rel>`, which `pipeline-run.sh resolve_rel` accepts, and does not fall back to the `overlay_fixture` evidence, so a run whose fixture lives only in the source tree FAILs `oracle_closed` with "does not resolve" although the overlay recorded where it is.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2010` — `corpus_sha256` reads the file through `read_regular` (O_NOFOLLOW, size-capped) and then re-opens it by path to hash; hash the bytes already read.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:536` — `poslist` nulls the whole `defects_missed_pm3_v1` list when one v1-only id's position exceeds `defects_seeded` (the grader maps such ids to their v1 position, `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1649-1656`); a v1 manifest with more defects than the current key loses the field entirely.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Security Audit Scope Analysis
# Two-Pass Methodology v1.0
#
# Shows file counts by security-relevant category to understand audit surface.
# Part of Loa's /audit skill enhancement.
#
# Usage: .claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh [OPTIONS]
#   --no-symlinks    Skip symlinks (default: follow)
#   --max-depth N    Limit search depth (default: unlimited)
#   --json           Output as JSON

set -euo pipefail

# Parse arguments
FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=true
MAX_DEPTH=""
OUTPUT_JSON=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case $1 in
    --no-symlinks) FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=false; shift ;;
    --max-depth) MAX_DEPTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) OUTPUT_JSON=true; shift ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

# Build find options as array (HIGH-002 remediation - prevents word splitting)
declare -a FIND_OPTS=(-type f)
if [[ "$FOLLOW_SYMLINKS" == "false" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-type f -not -type l)
fi
if [[ -n "$MAX_DEPTH" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-maxdepth "$MAX_DEPTH" "${FIND_OPTS[@]}")
fi

# Exclude patterns (POSIX compatible)
EXCLUDE_DIRS="node_modules|\.git|dist|build|\.next|vendor|__pycache__|\.venv"

# Count function with error suppression
# Uses array expansion for safe variable handling
count_files() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*.ts" -o -name "*.js" -o -name "*.py" -o -name "*.go" -o -name "*.java" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | \
    xargs grep -l "$pattern" 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

count_by_name() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*$pattern*" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

# Collect metrics
START_TIME=$(date +%s)

# Source files (entry points)
CONTROLLERS=$(count_by_name "controller")
ROUTES=$(count_by_name "route")
HANDLERS=$(count_by_name "handler")
API_ENDPOINTS=$(count_files 'app\.\(get\|post\|put\|delete\|patch\)\|router\.\(get\|post\)')

# Sink files (dangerous operations)
DB_QUERY=$(count_files '\.query\|\.execute\|SELECT\|INSERT\|UPDATE\|DELETE')
CMD_EXEC=$(count_files 'exec\|spawn\|system\|popen\|subprocess')
FILE_OPS=$(count_files 'readFile\|writeFile\|open(\|fs\.')

# Auth files
AUTH_FILES=$(count_files 'auth\|login\|session\|jwt\|token\|password')

# LLM/AI files
LLM_FILES=$(count_files 'openai\|anthropic\|llm\|prompt\|completion\|chat\|gpt\|claude')

END_TIME=$(date +%s)

+def split_segments(cmd):
+    """[(segment, separator after it)]: split on newline ; & | (&& || included) outside quotes and
+    parentheses; the separator is "|" for a pipe into the next segment, else ";" """
+    segs, cur, q, depth, i = [], [], None, 0, 0
+    while i < len(cmd):
+        ch = cmd[i]
+        if q == "'":
+            cur.append(ch)
+            if ch == "'":
+                q = None
+        elif q == '"':
+            cur.append(ch)
+            if ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(cmd):
+                cur.append(cmd[i + 1])
+                i += 1
+            elif ch == '"':
+                q = None
+        elif ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(cmd):
+            cur.append(ch + cmd[i + 1])
+            i += 1
+        elif ch in "'\"":
+            q = ch
+            cur.append(ch)
+        elif ch == "(":
+            depth += 1
+            cur.append(ch)
+        elif ch == ")":
+            depth = max(0, depth - 1)
+            cur.append(ch)
+        elif depth == 0 and ch in "\n;&|":
+            pipe = ch == "|" and cmd[i + 1:i + 2] != "|" and cmd[i - 1:i] != "|"
+            segs.append(("".join(cur), "|" if pipe else ";"))
+            cur = []
+        else:
+            cur.append(ch)
+        i += 1
+    segs.append(("".join(cur), ";"))
+    return [(x.strip(), sep) for x, sep in segs if x.strip()]

+    while w and w[0] in ("command", "env", "builtin", "exec", "nice"):
+        w = w[1:]

+            changed = True

+    a line that is not diff body and names a file (an `echo "=== $f"` marker); a header naming a target
+    (the longest one it holds) opens that target's section, any other header a dropped one; text before
+    the first header belongs to the sole target. Text no header attributes (several targets) is returned
+    as the loose list. Header lines are not part of a body. → (sections, loose)"""
+    out = {f: [] for f in targets}
+    loose = []
+    cur = targets[0] if len(targets) == 1 else None
+    buf = []

+    def flush():
+        if buf:
+            (out[cur] if cur is not None else loose).append("\n".join(buf))

+                flush()
+                buf = []
+                cur = hit

+        buf.append(line)

+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  dirty="$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .claude 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')" || dirty="?"
+  if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then printf '%s-dirty' "$head"; else printf '%s' "$head"; fi
+}

+def fixture_file(root, path):
+    """(bytes, exec) of a regular file at root/path with no symlink component, else None"""
+    cur = root
+    if os.path.islink(cur) or not os.path.isdir(cur):
+        return None
+    parts = path.split("/")
+    for c in parts:
+        cur = os.path.join(cur, c)
+        if os.path.islink(cur):
+            return None
+    try:
+        st = os.lstat(cur)
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
+        return None
+    return open(cur, "rb").read(), bool(st.st_mode & 0o111)
+
+def tree_blob(repo, commit, path):
+    """(bytes, exec, blob_id) of a regular-file entry in commit, else None"""
+    out = git(repo, "ls-tree", "-z", commit, "--", path)
+    if not out:
+        return None
+    ent = out.split(b"\0")[0].decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")
+    m = re.match(r"^(\d+) (\w+) ([0-9a-f]+)\t(.*)$", ent, re.S)
+    if not m or m.group(2) != "blob" or m.group(4) != path or m.group(1) not in ("100644", "100755"):
+        return None
+    data = git(repo, "cat-file", "blob", m.group(3))
+    if data is None:
+        return None
+    return data, m.group(1) == "100755", m.group(3)
+
+def expected(entries, mode, fixture, repo, meta):
+    """{path: (bytes, exec) | None}"""
+    exp = {}
+    for p, src in entries.items():
+        if src == "pr":
+            exp[p] = fixture_file(os.path.join(fixture, mode), p)
+        elif meta.get("head_available"):
+            tb = tree_blob(repo, meta["head_commit"], p)
+            exp[p] = (tb[0], tb[1]) if tb else None
+        else:
+            exp[p] = None
+    return exp
+
+def state(ws, path):
+    """sha256 of the sandbox file, 'absent', or a non-file marker (never followed)"""
+    cur = ws
+    for c in path.split("/")[:-1]:
+        cur = os.path.join(cur, c)
+        if os.path.islink(cur):
+            return "symlink-component"
+    full = os.path.join(ws, *path.split("/"))
+    if os.path.islink(full):
+        return "symlink"
+    if not os.path.lexists(full):
+        return "absent"
+    if not os.path.isfile(full):
+        return "not-a-file"
+    return sha(open(full, "rb").read())
+
+def safe_dst(ws, path):
+    cur = ws
+    for c in path.split("/")[:-1]:
+        cur = os.path.join(cur, c)
+        if os.path.islink(cur):
+            die("overlay refused: symlink component %s in the sandbox path of %s" % (os.path.relpath(cur, ws), path))
+        if os.path.lexists(cur) and not os.path.isdir(cur):
+            die("overlay refused: non-directory component %s in the sandbox path of %s" % (os.path.relpath(cur, ws), path))
+    return os.path.join(ws, *path.split("/"))
+
+def remove(dst):
+    if os.path.islink(dst) or (os.path.lexists(dst) and not os.path.isdir(dst)):
+        os.unlink(dst)
+    elif os.path.isdir(dst):
+        shutil.rmtree(dst)
+
+def gate_script(p):
+    return bool(re.match(r"^\.claude/(scripts|hooks)/", p) or re.match(r"^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$", p))
+
+def cmd_overlay(ws, fixture, mode, repo):
+    if mode not in ("head", "base"):
+        die("overlay mode must be head or base, got %r" % mode)
+    if not os.path.isdir(ws) or os.path.islink(ws):
+        die("workspace not found: " + ws)
+    entries, notes, meta = answer_set(fixture, repo)
+    exp = expected(entries, mode, fixture, repo, meta)
+    for n in notes:
+        note("overlay: " + n)
+    if entries and any(s == "fix" for s in entries.values()) and not meta.get("head_available"):
+        note("overlay: head_commit %s unavailable: fix-commit paths outside the PR are removed" % meta.get("head_commit"))
+    lines, gates, removed = [], [], 0

+        remove(dst)

+def read_evidence(f):
+    ev = {"overlay_sha256": {}}

+        line = line.rstrip("\n")
+        if "=" not in line:

+        elif k not in ev:

+    return ev

+    ev = read_evidence(evfile)
+    mo = ev.get("mount_overlay", "")
+    m = re.match(r"^(head|base):(\d+)$", mo)
+    if not m:
+        print("FAIL (a) -: mount_overlay=%s (want head|base:<n>)" % (mo or "<missing>")); sys.exit(1)
+    mode, n = m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
+    entries, _notes, meta = answer_set(fixture, repo)
+    exp = expected(entries, mode, fixture, repo, meta)
+    fails = []
+    if n != len(entries):
+        fails.append(("a", "-", "mount_overlay names %d paths, the fixture's answer set has %d" % (n, len(entries))))
+    rec = ev["overlay_sha256"]
+    present = 0
+    for p in sorted(entries):
+        want = sha(exp[p][0]) if exp[p] is not None else "absent"
+        got = state(ws, p)
+        if got != "absent":
+            present += 1
+        if p not in rec:
+            fails.append(("c", p, "no overlay_sha256 line"))
+            if got != want:
+                fails.append(("a", p, "state %s, want %s (%s)" % (got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+            continue
+        if got != rec[p]:
+            if rec[p] == want:
+                fails.append(("c", p, "mount_mutated=%s (pre-run %s, now %s)" % (p, rec[p][:12], got[:12])))
+            else:
+                fails.append(("a", p, "pre-run %s, now %s, want %s (%s)" % (rec[p][:12], got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+        elif got != want:
+            fails.append(("a", p, "state %s, want %s (%s)" % (got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+    # (b) later-only pinned versions
+    if not has_commit(repo, source_commit):

+        later = {}
+    else:

+                if ff is not None:
+                    known.add(sha(ff[0]))
+        later = {}
+        for p in sorted(entries):

+            if tb is None or len(tb[0]) == 0:
+                continue
+            h = sha(tb[0])
+            if h in known:
+                continue
+            later.setdefault(h, (p, len(tb[0]), tb[2]))
+        sizes = set(v[1] for v in later.values())
+        scanned = 0

+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  dirty="$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .claude 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')" || dirty="?"
+  if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then printf '%s-dirty' "$head"; else printf '%s' "$head"; fi
+}

+overlay_answer_paths() {

+  local cs
+  cs="$(_sm_copy_source "$tree")"
+  _sm_evidence copy_source "$cs"
+  if [[ ! "$cs" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
+    _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: copy source $tree is not a clean git tree (copy_source=$cs)"; return 2
+  fi
+  if [[ -n "$want" && "$cs" != "$want" ]]; then
+    _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: copy_source $cs differs from source_commit $want"; return 2
+  fi
+  local out line rc=0
+  out="$(_sm_oracle_py overlay "$ws" "$fixture" "$mode" "$tree")" || rc=$?
+  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: the overlay failed (exit $rc)"; return 2; }
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [[ "$line" == *=* ]] || continue
+    _sm_evidence "${line%%=*}" "${line#*=}"
+  done <<<"$out"
+  _sm_evidence overlay_fixture "$fixture"
+  _sm_evidence overlay_source_tree "$tree"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# check_mount_closed <ws> <fixture-dir> [<source-tree>] [<evidence-file>]
+check_mount_closed() {
+  local ws="$1" fixture="${2:-}" tree="${3:-${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}}" evf="${4:-${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}}"
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$fixture" && -f "$fixture/head.diff" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: fixture not found or has no head.diff: ${fixture:-<none>}"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$evf" && -f "$evf" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: no evidence file (ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE)"; return 2; }
+  local cs out rc=0
+  cs="$(sed -n 's/^copy_source=//p' "$evf" | sed -n '1p')"
+  [[ "$cs" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: no clean copy_source in the evidence (got '${cs:-none}')"; return 2; }
+  out="$(_sm_oracle_py check "$ws" "$fixture" "$evf" "$tree" "$cs")" || rc=$?
+  if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then

+}

+apply_eval_config_variant() {

+       && "$(G="$g" yq -r '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_cents_max' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == 600 ]] \
+      || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: $g budget keys did not take effect"; return 2; }
+  done

+  return 0
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# evals/tests/sandbox-mount.bats — cycle-131 Sprint 263 Task 1.1 (PRD FR-1 AC 1, AC 5;
+# FR-5 AC 1; SDD §5.2 overlay_answer_paths / check_mount_closed, D-1.1, D-5.x)
+#
+# evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh's closed mount on a fixture-shaped sandbox: a
+# throwaway source repository (the pinned Loa tree: a head commit, then a fix commit
+# that is the pin), a PR fixture (head.diff, head/, base/, fixture.yaml) whose head.diff
+# carries every path shape (modified, added, deleted, renamed, a quoted path with a
+# space, a symlink in head, a path outside .claude/, a removed hunk line that looks like
+# a header, a binary hunk), and a sandbox built as pipeline-run.sh builds it (pr/ copied,
+# a base commit, the whole .claude/ mounted). Also the cycle-131 toggles (bare_model,
+# dissent, oracle_open) and the eval config variant. No model call, no docker.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+  LIB="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sm.XXXXXX")"
+  SRC="$T/src" FX="$T/fx" W="$T/ws"
+  export ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE="$T/ev.txt"; : > "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
+  make_source
+  make_fixture
+  make_ws
+}
+
+teardown() {
+  chmod -R u+rwx "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
+  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+g() { git -C "$1" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t -c commit.gpgsign=false "${@:2}"; }
+
+# the pinned Loa tree: commit H (= the PR's head_commit) then commit F (the fix, the pin)

# tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget-scale.bats — cycle-131 Sprint 1 Task 1.8 (PRD FR-4, SDD D-4.2).
#

# (default 600). With diff the gate's budget is min(max(budget_cents, ceil(estimate × 1.2)), budget_cents_max); an
# estimate above that still refuses (exit 4, status budget_exceeded, reason budget). A malformed scale or maximum
# fails closed to fixed. The envelope names budget_scale / budget_cents_effective / budget_cents_max only when the

#

# tokens = diff bytes / 3 + 500 (the gate's own estimate) — 108,300 bytes → 366c, 62,700 → 214c, 208,500 → 700c.
# =============================================================================

load adversarial-review-s3-helpers

setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3bsc; }
teardown() { s3_teardown; }

flatline_protocol:

${3:-}"
}

content.content:
# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

---

## Architecture Rubrics

### ARCH-MO: Modularity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Clear separation of concerns. Well-defined interfaces. Easy to modify/extend. |
| 4 | Good modularity with minor coupling issues. |
| 3 | Some modularity but tight coupling in places. |
| 2 | Poor separation. Components heavily interdependent. |
| 1 | Monolithic. No clear boundaries. |

### ARCH-SC: Scalability
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Horizontally scalable. Stateless services. Caching strategy. Database sharding ready. |
| 4 | Mostly scalable with minor bottlenecks. |
| 3 | Can scale vertically but horizontal scaling problematic. |
| 2 | Scalability issues. Single points of failure. |

# Sprint 1 Security Audit Feedback

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)
**Change under audit:** `pr/head.diff` — cycle-131 sprint-263: closed review-catch mount, grader 1.3.0 (three results, oracle detector), dissent line anchors + budget_scale, curated multi-site labels, versioned re-grade; 35 files
**Task:** review-r27

---

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

---

## Scope and prerequisites

- **Prerequisite deviation (recorded).** Phase 0 of this skill expects `engineer-feedback.md` to read "All good" before an audit runs. The review's verdict is CHANGES_REQUIRED (2 HIGH). The task brief instructs the audit to run regardless and autonomously, so it ran; the review's two HIGH findings were re-verified independently here (one by an executable reproduction) rather than carried over.
- **Inputs read.** `pr/head.diff` in full; every touched file under `pr/head/` where a finding sits; `pr/base/` for the before-state of `adversarial-review.sh`, the grader and the pipeline; `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md` and `adversarial-review.json` (the review's dissent, 7 findings, 0 rejected); the security dissent envelope written by this audit. `grimoires/loa/known-failures.md` is unreadable in this workspace (session hook warning); triage ran without it.
- **Executable evidence.** The workspace holds no `tests/` or `evals/` tree, so 9 of the 10 bats suites the PR touches cannot run here (their helpers and fixtures are absent). `evals/tests/sandbox-mount.bats` needs only the mount library, git, yq and python3, so it was run on a copy of `pr/head/`: 11 ok, 1 skipped (the real-corpus case, no clone). A two-case reproduction suite was appended to the same fixture builders (see HIGH-001). The grader's Python scope code, the oracle detector's `split_segments`, the class 7 exemption and the yq `//` read were each executed in isolation with the inputs named in the findings.
- **Trust assumptions.** The PR fixture (`evals/fixtures/review-prs/pr-NN/`), the suite root, the source tree and `meta/arm-evidence.txt` are harness-owned and trusted. Everything under `<run-dir>/sandbox/` (including `sandbox/pr/`, `sandbox/.loa.config.yaml`, `sandbox/.git`) is agent-writable and UNTRUSTED. The dissent voices' payloads are untrusted model output.
- **Scope limits.** `Unable to assess`: whether the container executor leaves the sandbox owned by another uid (which would make the post-run `git` reads in clause (d) fail on `safe.directory`); no run directory is available here. Noted under Observations, not tallied.

## Executive Summary

The security posture of the change is sound where it defends the trust boundary it names: the overlay never follows a symlink, the fixture is read with `O_NOFOLLOW` and size caps, `git` runs with an isolated config and `core.fsmonitor=false`, paths are normalised before use and `.claude/checksums.json` stays harness-owned. The budget scaling is off by default and the envelope is byte-identical without the key. No secrets, no injection path and no network sink were introduced.

Two defects block the merge and both were confirmed by execution. The closed-mount wiring records the answer-path digests, then lets `apply_arm_toggles` rewrite `SKILL.md` frontmatter and `model-config.yaml`, then verifies against the recorded digests: on arm `a7_effort_medium` any review-catch PR whose answer set holds a skill with an `effort:` line is refused as `infrastructure_error` before a phase runs (reproduced: `FAIL (c) .claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md: mount_mutated`). The grader's 1.3.0 same-scope rule ends a Python definition at the `):` of a multi-line signature, so black-formatted functions have no scope and the decision statistic under-credits on a common code shape (reproduced: a three-line signature's def "ends" on line 3).

Six MEDIUM findings follow, three of them trust-boundary issues the eval harness explicitly set out to close: the row writer classifies a missing dissent as "planned" from the agent-writable sandbox config; the new KF-046 class 7 exemption treats a live `WebFetch` of an upstream URL as "quoting PR content" whenever that URL appears in a fixture file; and the `diff` budget scaling silently undoes the documented fail-closed 0-cent spend cap. Fourteen LOW findings complete the list.

**Security Issues Found:**
| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 2 |
| Medium | 6 |
| Low | 14 |

---

## Critical Security Issues (Must Fix)

None.

---

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] Arm toggles rewrite overlaid answer paths after their digests are recorded and before the closed-mount check

**Severity:** HIGH — **Confidence:** high (reproduced)
**File:** `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:566` (order); `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:356-361` (mutation); `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:986` (refusal)
**Issue:** `pipeline-run.sh` runs `lib_call overlay_answer_paths` (:559), which prints one `overlay_sha256=<path>=<sha>` line per answer path, then `lib_call apply_arm_toggles "$WS" "$TOGGLES" "$ARM"` (:566), then `lib_call check_mount_closed` (:577). The `effort` toggle rewrites every sandbox skill in place:
```bash
      effort)
        local f total=0 stripped=0 still=""
        for f in "$ws"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
          ...
          if [[ "$(_sm_strip_frontmatter_effort "$f")" == "1" ]]; then stripped=$((stripped + 1)); fi
```
(`head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:356-361`) and `yq -i` edits `.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml` (:373). Clause (c) of `cmd_check` then compares the current state with the recorded digest and, because the recorded digest equals the fixture's version, reports the toggle's edit as tampering:
```python
            if rec[p] == want:
                fails.append(("c", p, "mount_mutated=%s (pre-run %s, now %s)" % (p, rec[p][:12], got[:12])))
```
(`head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:985-986`). `lib_call` turns the non-zero exit into `infra` (`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:469`).
**Reproduction:** appended to the PR's own `sandbox-mount.bats` fixture builders (a `SKILL.md` answer path with `effort: high` in its frontmatter): overlay → `apply_arm_toggles '{"effort":"medium"}'` → `check_mount_closed` exits 2 with `ERROR: check_mount_closed: FAIL (c) .claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md: mount_mutated=.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md (pre-run a77faa5262bf, now ae57fcfa6cc5)`; the control case without the toggle passes.
**Impact:** `a7_effort_medium` has `task_types: [all]` (`head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:89`). Six skills in this tree carry an `effort:` line (auditing-security, bridgebuilder-review, designing-architecture, implementing-tasks, red-teaming, reviewing-code); any review-catch PR touching one of them (the AG-50 test names `auditing-security/SKILL.md` in pr-04's answer set) or `model-config.yaml` makes every A7 trial an `infrastructure_error` with no phase run. The pre-registered A7 contrast silently loses those cells; `took-effect` pauses nothing because no run exists. The same class applies to `audit_delta_instruction` (rewrites `auditing-security/SKILL.md`, :340-346), `karpathy_block` (`.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md`, :316) and `rule_files` (`.claude/rules/*`, :336) on any arm that carries them for a review-catch task. The only test of toggle/overlay interaction (`head/evals/tests/sandbox-mount.bats:302`) uses `dissent: false`, which edits `.loa.config.yaml`, outside the answer set. The header comment "the checked surface is the launched one" (`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:575`) shows the ordering is deliberate, so this is a design conflict rather than a slip.
